patch.value: GH-1136: npm 12 object-form npm pack receipts break registry package installs

Track GitHub issue #1136: npm 12 changed `npm pack --json` from an array to an object keyed by package name. The package-source parser accepts only the older array shape and then misclassifies valid but unrecognized JSON as a line-oriented filename, producing a tar path ending in `}` and breaking every explicit npm extension install.

Parse npm 11 array and npm 12 object receipts through one typed SDK-owned contract; select the requested entry deterministically; never apply a filename fallback after JSON parsed successfully; add npm 11/12 unit, integration, packed-consumer, and negative malformed-shape coverage; preserve actionable structured CLI errors.
npm 12.0.2, Node 26.5.0, Linux; explicit npm: package sources
Run `pm package install npm:pm-brief` under npm 12.0.2; observe the valid object-form pack receipt fall through to a tarball path named `}`.

The package source accepts every documented npm pack JSON shape, selects the requested package deterministically, and fails closed with a shape-specific diagnostic when well-formed JSON is unsupported.
Object-form npm 12 receipts are ignored after successful JSON parsing; the last pretty-printed line `}` is treated as a filename and tar fails with ENOENT.
All explicit registry extension installs are broken for users on current npm 12, including every published first-party package.
